name: Wilsonian idealism
summary: Wilsonian idealism holds that US and world foreign policy should rest on moral principle: national self-determination, democracy, open diplomacy, freer trade, reduced armaments and a general association of nations that guarantees the independence of all states. It treats democracy as the most virtuous government and sees collective security, not balance of power, as the route to peace.
scope: The foreign-policy doctrine drawn from Woodrow Wilson's 1917-1919 war aims, centrally the Fourteen Points of 8 January 1918 and the League of Nations project, as described in scholarly accounts. It does not cover Wilson's domestic record on race or his Latin American interventions as doctrine, and domestic and social statements are mostly low-confidence inferences from his Progressive New Freedom liberalism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a Wilsonian concern; Progressive-era liberalism leaned toward some social reform, so a mild lean toward agreeing is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the New Freedom's Progressive reform temper; the doctrine itself is about foreign affairs and says nothing on wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Wilson wanted competition restored at home yet also business serving the public interest, so adherents are split and the doctrine is silent.

public-ownership.rationale: The New Freedom sought restored competition rather than nationalisation, so public ownership is inferred as disfavoured.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Wilson-era liberals backed a graduated income tax but the doctrine is silent on how high; no clear lean.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from Progressive-era liberalism's tolerance of organised labour; not a defining Wilsonian position.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not addressed by Wilsonian foreign-policy doctrine; liberal respect for property is balanced by Progressive regulation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The New Freedom wanted business to serve the public interest rather than dominate it, implying tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: Progressive liberalism was not hostile to social provision; the doctrine does not address welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Reform liberalism of Wilson's type kept private enterprise; worker ownership is not part of it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The doctrine never addressed surveillance; liberal civil-liberty concerns pull against wartime security instincts.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine and anachronistic to its era; no basis for a lean.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the liberal internationalist tradition has no settled view on it.

strong-leader.rationale: Wilsonianism is committed to constitutional democracy; Wilson himself favoured strong presidential leadership, so only a mild disagreement is inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Wilsonianism builds on the state and on international organisation, and treats democratic government as the most virtuous form.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; no basis for a lean.

empower-police-military.rationale: Point IV of the Fourteen Points calls for armaments cut to the lowest level consistent with domestic safety.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Progressive-era moral reform leaned against it but Wilsonianism is silent.

decide-locally.rationale: The doctrine centres on national and international institutions rather than devolution; a mild lean from that emphasis.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from Progressive-era reform liberalism; not a doctrinal matter.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed by Wilsonian doctrine; adherents are not defined by a family-values position.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic to the era; modern liberal internationalists lean yes but the doctrine does not address it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; no basis for a lean.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wilson's moralism had Presbyterian roots, but the doctrine does not call for a larger public religious role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Wilson's own record was segregationist and scholars debate his racialised self-determination, so adherents are genuinely split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Self-determination respects national aspirations, but the doctrine does not make cultural preservation a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: Wilsonians sought a new international order yet through institutions and treaties; no clear lean.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration policy is not part of the doctrine; no basis for a lean.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Point XIV calls for a general association of nations to guarantee all states, and Wilson championed the League as the core of the order.

free-trade.rationale: Point III calls for removing economic barriers and equal trade conditions among nations, and free trade is listed among Wilsonian aims.

nation-first.rationale: Wilsonianism rejects isolationism and puts cooperation through a league of nations ahead of narrow national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Scholars link Wilsonianism to humanitarian intervention, though Wilson himself envisioned no direct US shaping of other states, so only mild agreement.

open-borders.rationale: Borders and migration are not addressed; the doctrine presupposes nation-states.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; Wilson-era liberalism assumed growth and trade, so it would disagree.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic to the doctrine, though modern liberal internationalists favour multilateral climate action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; Wilsonian optimism is about institutions and democracy, not technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic to Wilson; the doctrine says nothing on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Wilson's order rests on democratic self-determination and law; he opposed Bolshevik revolution, so revolution is mildly disfavoured.

experts-over-public.rationale: Wilson the political scientist valued expertise, but the doctrine rests on democratic consent; adherents split.

central-planning.rationale: The New Freedom sought restored competition and Wilsonianism endorses capitalism and free trade, not planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine favours capitalism, so worker or public ownership as a condition is not part of it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; no basis for a lean.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed by the doctrine.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Wilson cut tariffs at home and Point III demands the removal of economic barriers between nations.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Wilsonianism favours open trade and capitalism over state-directed industrial policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The New Freedom favoured small competitors against trusts, but the doctrine does not state a property position.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wilsonianism endorses capitalism; abolishing money and wage labour is outside it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Wilson created the Federal Reserve; the doctrine itself is silent, so a mild inference.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not part of Wilsonian doctrine, which is liberal-democratic.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wilsonianism holds democracy to be the most virtuous government for every nation.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Wilson's war aims opposed autocracy; he held democracy the best form, though Point XII and others tolerate varied governments.

democracy-best.rationale: Per the foreign-relations account, Wilson considered democracy the most virtuous form of government, fit for every nation.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; Wilson-era Progressives backed initiative and referendum in places but the doctrine is silent.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils replacing parliaments are the Bolshevik model Wilson opposed in favour of democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Self-determination supports national independence, but Point X sought autonomy within Austria-Hungary, not full secession; split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Wilsonianism rests on democratic consent, so inherent ruling capacity is disfavoured, though Wilson's racial views complicate this.

political-violence-never.rationale: Wilson accepted war for democratic ends but stressed lawful change; adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Wilsonianism seeks peace through collective security and arms reduction, not war as a virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic principles; Wilson's personal religiosity tempered this.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Wilson's moralism was religiously informed, but the doctrine bases order on democratic consent and international law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Wilsonianism centres on collective security through a public association of nations.

military-superiority.rationale: Point IV seeks mutual arms reduction; superiority over rivals runs against that and against collective security.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Point IX adjusts frontiers along national lines yet Point X keeps multinational states; adherents split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Wilsonian liberalism sees progress through democratic institutions, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberal reformism emphasises opportunity; the doctrine does not address outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Wilson's domestic record on this was poor.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Point V asks for impartial colonial settlement weighting colonial populations, but nothing about reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Wilsonianism builds a universal association of nations, not blocs of shared civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine stresses moral duty in foreign policy but is silent on personal ethics.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Wilsonianism is rights-based and liberal, not communitarian.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Wilsonianism embraces trade, capitalism and progress, so rejection of industrial civilisation is alien to it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; democratic consent is central to the doctrine.

restore-past-order.rationale: Wilsonianism aims to build a new international order, not to restore a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wilson was both a moralist and a pragmatist; scholars debate whether he was a 'higher realist', so adherents split.

direct-action.rationale: The doctrine works through treaties, elections and institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Wilson insisted on open, frank diplomacy and on moral standards in foreign relations; inferred agreement.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly alien to a progressive, trade-embracing doctrine.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Alien to Wilsonianism, which endorses capitalism and trade.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist principle not part of Wilsonian liberalism.

production-for-use.rationale: Wilsonianism endorses capitalism and market trade.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim that Wilsonian liberalism rejects.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Wilson opposed Bolshevism and champions democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: Alien to a liberal capitalist doctrine.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Wilsonianism holds that free trade and democracy promote peace, the opposite view.

taxation-theft.rationale: Wilsonian liberalism accepts a legitimate state and taxation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Wilsonianism ties rights to nations as well as individuals, via national self-determination.

conscription.rationale: Wilson's government used conscription in 1917, but the doctrine does not require it; split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Doctrine prizes democratic voice and participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which prizes public interest.

positive-liberty.rationale: Progressive liberalism leaned to this, but the doctrine does not address it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Wilson held racist views personally, but scholars distinguish the doctrine; modern adherents reject it, so a mild disagreement.

total-state.rationale: Opposed to democratic self-government and the liberal order Wilsonianism defends.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a Wilsonian theme; the doctrine is internationalist and gradualist.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Wilsonianism opposes conquest and seeks guarantees of territorial integrity for all states.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal in form; opposed to democratic consent.

bound-labor.rationale: Incompatible with a liberal democratic doctrine.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Wilsonianism assumes universal principles that reason and diplomacy can establish.

universal-morality.rationale: Wilson believed nations should meet high moral standards and that democracy is fit for every nation, implying universal principles.

single-common-good.rationale: Wilson spoke of a common interest of mankind but the doctrine works through balancing of national interests in a league; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Wilson endorsed the Balfour Declaration but it is not a doctrinal matter.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Fourteen Points say nothing on diaspora citizenship, so adherents have no settled view.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed by Wilsonian foreign-policy doctrine.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance was outside Wilson's foreign-policy doctrine, so no position follows.

economic-freedom.rationale: Wilsonianism pairs political liberty with open trade and capitalism; mild agreement inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Wilson stressed moral example in foreign policy but legal institutions too; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wilsonianism is defined by self-determination, and the Fourteen Points apply it to Poland, the Balkans, Ottoman peoples and others.

force-without-un.rationale: Wilsonianism is committed to collective action through an association of nations rather than unilateral force, though Wilson himself intervened in Latin America.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Wilson's outlook was religious as well as rational; the doctrine does not demand reason only.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The doctrine never discusses welfare eligibility for immigrants, so no position is inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare conditions are a later debate that Wilsonian doctrine does not touch.

class-collaboration.rationale: Wilson's New Freedom wanted business to serve the public interest, implying cooperation over class conflict; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Wilsonianism favours a universal association of nations, not fronts against Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: Wilsonianism is nation-based but liberal; this idea is not part of it.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Wilson-era views varied; not part of the doctrine.

ban-interest.rationale: Alien to a capitalist, trade-embracing doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Wilson's own administration segregated federal offices, but this was not part of the idealist doctrine, and adherents are now opposed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis that Wilsonian liberal democratic doctrine rejects.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in Wilsonianism.

national-mission.rationale: Wilson held democracy suited every nation and gave the US a moral mandate to lead, though Slaughter notes he did not plan active export; mild agreement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not a theme; Wilsonians trust democratic institutions.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Wilson signed eugenics-adjacent measures as governor, but the doctrine does not address it; adherents split.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from rule-of-law and open-diplomacy liberalism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wilsonianism supports an active state domestically and international bodies abroad.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; a modern adherent rejects it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Self-determination and the equal weight given to populations in Point V imply equal standing; Wilson's own racial record makes this contested.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist debate with no Wilsonian view; socialism itself is rejected.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Point V weighs colonial peoples' interests, but the doctrine does not characterise settler states, so adherents are split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions within states fall outside a doctrine about relations among nations.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in schools is a domestic question the doctrine does not address; Wilson's own faith pulls both ways.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis foreign to Wilsonianism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Wilsonian self-determination rests on peoples governing themselves, and Point V gives populations equal weight with governments.

trade-surplus.rationale: Point III's equal trade conditions favour open exchange, not mercantilist surplus-seeking.

population-transfer.rationale: Opposed to Wilsonian protection of national minorities and territorial integrity.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Wilsonians condemn aggression but accept force through collective security.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Wilsonianism pursues cooperation among nations rather than struggle between peoples.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept not part of Wilsonian doctrine.

separated-powers.rationale: Wilson favoured checks in a democratic order, though he criticised the US system; inferred mild agreement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Wilsonian doctrine states no ranking of the poor's needs; New Freedom reform was aimed at competition rather than poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A modern British housing policy with no connection to Wilsonian doctrine.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour-law detail that the foreign-policy doctrine never addresses.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The doctrine's frontier-drawing on national lines (Points IX, X) does not amount to a view on diversity and cohesion.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Wilsonian liberalism values legal protections, though Wilson's wartime administration curbed dissent; mild disagreement.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; wartime Wilson administration used controls, but not as doctrine.

party-controls-media.rationale: Open covenants and public diplomacy imply openness; control of media is contrary to liberal democracy.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are a domestic matter the doctrine ignores.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Legislators' pay is not a theme in Wilson's war aims or New Freedom reforms.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is outside Wilsonian foreign-policy doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Point XIV's association of nations with mutual guarantees implies some pooling, though the League was not a supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; the US president commands forces, but not as doctrine.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is unrelated to the doctrine, though Wilson was a Presbyterian, not an episcopalian.

clerical-rule.rationale: Opposed to democracy as best government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Wilsonians backed the war effort as a fight for democracy.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Liberal democracy; Wilson's wartime censorship was not doctrine.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term rules are not addressed by the doctrine; Wilson himself considered a third term but it was no doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Progressives backed recall but the doctrine is silent.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Wilson opposed isolationism, though also criticised old balance-of-power alliances in favour of a general league.

people-in-arms.rationale: Doctrine seeks arms reduction and collective security.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The doctrine has no view on rural versus urban morality.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Point VIII and IX redraw borders along national lines; no general reunification principle.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Wilson was an academic; not a Wilsonian theme.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Wilson's universal-democracy claim implies a hierarchy of governments, but the doctrine does not address cultures; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not part of Wilson's international programme, so no position is inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic to the 1918 programme, which concerns international order.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship of pornography is not discussed in the doctrine; Progressive moral reform leaned both ways.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Point IX adjusts frontiers along national lines, but citizenship rules are not discussed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Point X and XII seek autonomy for nationalities; language not addressed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemption from general laws is a domestic legal question the doctrine does not address.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: J. S. Mill-style individuality is not found in Wilson's war aims, so no position follows.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not a Wilsonian aim; the order assumes financial obligations.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Wilsonianism sees political self-determination as primary and endorses capitalism.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Wilsonianism holds democracy to be the most virtuous government.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate Wilson's death in 1924, so this is anachronistic and uninferrable.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Wilson-era liberals took no doctrinal stand on how heads of state are chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Wilson signed the Federal Reserve Act, but the doctrine says nothing on central-bank independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Wilsonian settlement of disputes through negotiation and national frontiers, not retaining claimed territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Wilson wanted business to serve the public interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist dispute on classifying the USSR with no Wilsonian position.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine postdates Wilson and is not addressed.

collective-defense.rationale: Point XIV calls for mutual guarantees of political independence and territorial integrity among states, the logic of collective security.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Point VII and VIII call for restoration of invaded territory and national consent; inferred application.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state power is not addressed by the doctrine, and Wilson's faith complicates any inference.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Wilson led his party as a partisan president, but the doctrine does not hold a view on ceremonial heads of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; split between self-determination and territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Point X on autonomy for Austria-Hungary's peoples is loosely related, but no clear position follows.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wilson signed a graduated income tax in 1913, but the doctrine is silent on tax rates, so no lean is inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is not part of Wilsonian doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Wilsonian order rests on international covenants binding states.

space-expansion.rationale: Space travel is anachronistic to Wilson's era and doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not part of Wilson's foreign-policy programme.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are outside the doctrine.

refugee-return.rationale: Wilson's points call for restoration of invaded territories such as Belgium but not for refugee return rights, so no clear position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Wilsonianism rejects conquest; frontiers only adjusted along national lines by peaceful settlement.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in the Fourteen Points, which call only for lower trade barriers.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Wilsonianism seeks a universal association, not ethnic unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Point X wanted autonomy for the peoples of Austria-Hungary, but also states of their own for Poland and others; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The doctrine does not address minority strategy between emigration and local rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Wilsonian idealism holds that ideas and moral purpose drive change; the name itself signals this.

ban-cartels.rationale: The New Freedom sought to break monopolies and restore competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank bailouts are a later debate; the doctrine says nothing on them.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Wilsonianism is liberal democratic, not majoritarian absolutism.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Point III calls for equal trade conditions and removal of economic barriers, the opposite of closed imperial blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Point III wants equal trade conditions; binding standards are not discussed and are anachronistic.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foquismo is the opposite of Wilsonian reliance on democratic consent and lawful international order.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Wilsonian democracy and its war aims against autocracy imply opposition to hereditary rank, though the doctrine does not address titles directly.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curricula are outside the doctrine, which is internationalist but silent on teaching.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Scholars note Wilson's self-determination was racially differentiated and tolerated imperial rule, yet Point V weighs colonial peoples' interests equally; adherents split, leaning against.

patriotic-education.rationale: Wilson stressed loyalty in wartime yet the doctrine is internationalist; split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic to the doctrine, which does not address it.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; Wilson created the Federal Reserve but that is not doctrine.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Wilsonianism endorses capitalism and assumes it can be reformed, as the New Freedom's restored competition shows.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Wilsonianism opposes imperial spheres of influence in favour of equal standing of nations.

delink-world-market.rationale: Wilsonianism wants removal of trade barriers and integration, as in Point III.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that Wilsonian liberalism rejects, since it holds trade benefits all.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not a Wilsonian aim, though historic Wilson allowed segregation.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Point V seeks impartial adjustment of colonial claims, not voiding of treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democracy is the best government in Wilsonian thought.

minority-veto.rationale: Collective action in an association of nations implies binding decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from consent of the governed principle.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Wilson admired parliamentary government in his scholarship, but the doctrine does not rule on monarch versus legislature.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed by Wilsonian doctrine.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed by Wilsonian doctrine.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The doctrine states no duty of the wealthy toward the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Wilsonians believe in active engagement abroad and at home.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not part of the doctrine.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Wilsonianism holds that free trade is beneficial, the opposite of dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Eligibility for office is not addressed in Wilson's programme.

party-own-road.rationale: An intra-communist debate that carries no Wilsonian position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid and self-reliance are not discussed in the 1918 doctrine.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Wilsonian peaceful settlement; Point VIII endorsed return of Alsace-Lorraine, so some split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The doctrine does not address settler-indigenous relations, and Wilson's own record offers no guide.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic to a doctrine that predates fascism and totalitarian communism's maturity.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Wilson held Lost Cause views, but the doctrine does not address it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A modern debate on monuments that the doctrine does not address.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: A modern debate absent from Wilsonian doctrine.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A modern debate absent from Wilsonian doctrine.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Wilsonianism holds democracy to be fit for every nation.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care-work wages are not addressed in the doctrine.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations are not addressed in the doctrine.

office-by-exam.rationale: Wilson favoured civil-service merit hiring in the Progressive tradition, but the doctrine does not frame it as an exam system, so no position.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Wilsonian free trade implies openness to foreign investment.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed by the doctrine.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is not discussed; Wilsonian representative democracy is silent here.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not part of the doctrine.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from consent of the governed.

single-official-language.rationale: Points X and XII ask autonomy for nationalities, but language policy is not discussed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Wilsonian free trade and openness imply against it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A later US legal doctrine, anachronistic to Wilson's programme.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Wilsonianism says nothing on consumption and status goods.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Wilsonianism prefers collective legal means; Wilson also intervened in Mexico, so only mild.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Violates guarantees of territorial independence and national self-determination.

corporate-influence.rationale: The New Freedom opposed business domination of government.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not addressed in the doctrine.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not addressed in the doctrine.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort policy is not part of Wilson's programme.

democratic-peace.rationale: Wilsonianism holds that spreading democracy and a league of free nations secures peace; Wilson saw the League as democracy applied globally.

non-intervention.rationale: Wilsonianism supports collective action and humanitarian intervention, so it rejects a ban for any reason.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a labour-movement debate not addressed by the doctrine.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not addressed by the doctrine.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Point I demands that diplomacy proceed frankly and in public view, an open-government principle.

local-production.rationale: Wilsonian free trade favours exchange across borders.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Wilsonianism wants international covenants binding states.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Wilsonianism wants equal standing of large and small states under Point XIV.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not addressed in the doctrine.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The doctrine does not discuss the socialist distinction between personal and productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Wilson opposed Bolshevism but the doctrine does not frame a crusade; split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Health and service delivery models are not addressed by the doctrine.

religion-illusion.rationale: Wilson's moralism was Christian; Marxist view rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Scholarly accounts list capitalism among Wilsonian commitments.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Wilson's doctrine does not address women's equality, so no position is inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare is not part of the doctrine.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not addressed, though self-determination is about political rather than linguistic rule.

treaties-binding.rationale: Wilsonian order depends on covenants being kept; inferred to domestic treaties.

majority-settlement.rationale: Opposed to Wilsonian protection of national minorities.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Wilsonian self-determination rests on the living population's consent.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; historical fact.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic to the doctrine, which concerns international order.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Point V requires colonial populations' interests have equal weight with the colonial government's.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic legal question the doctrine does not address.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine favours representative democracy but does not rule on direct participation in workplaces.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An intersectional framework is anachronistic to Wilson's programme.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics is outside the doctrine.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Wilsonians do not make claims on the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to Wilsonianism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Wilsonianism holds democracy fit for every nation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Wilson's Presbyterianism complicates this but the doctrine rests on popular consent.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not addressed by the doctrine.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern workplace-law question absent from the doctrine.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ordoliberal synthesis is not found in Wilson's programme, which endorses capitalism and trade but does not specify a social model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Point IV seeks reduction of arms to the lowest point consistent with domestic safety, not abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Sequential development theory is not addressed in the doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Wilsonianism is against both isolationism and balance-of-power blocs, favouring a general league.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit schemes are not addressed in the doctrine.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF conditionality postdates Wilson, so the doctrine gives no guide.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is anachronistic to the doctrine.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to Wilsonianism.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Open covenants and international law imply rule by public standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Wilsonianism supports democracy; racial franchise contradicts consent of the governed.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is anachronistic to a 1918 doctrine.

open-government-data.rationale: Point I's public diplomacy suggests transparency; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based deliberation is not addressed by the doctrine.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Theological reform is not part of the doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The New Freedom opposed economic concentration.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic to the doctrine, though modern liberal internationalists lean yes.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Contrary to Wilson's religious moralism and liberal principles.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; Points X and XII on autonomy for nationalities hint at it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The doctrine makes no comparison of charity and state aid.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits for legislators are not discussed in the doctrine.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is anachronistic to Wilsonian doctrine.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction-risk policy is anachronistic to Wilsonian doctrine.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Church office rules are not addressed by the doctrine.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority law is not addressed by the doctrine.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Resident-alien suffrage is not addressed by the doctrine.

rent-control.rationale: Rent regulation is not addressed by the doctrine.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is anachronistic to the doctrine.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Basing rights are not addressed in the Fourteen Points, so no position is inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The doctrine predates the legal concept of genocide.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The doctrine takes no position on returns to ownership versus labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Wilsonianism backs force in collective security and defence.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist-theory debate absent from Wilsonian doctrine.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Wilson's moral framing is notable, but not a spiritual struggle of good and evil as doctrine; split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A diaspora-Zionism debate the doctrine does not enter.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology of God's gender is not addressed by the doctrine.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is not addressed by the doctrine.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Wilsonianism protects minorities and open trade.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative unification of a people is not discussed, though Points IX and XIII follow national lines.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socialist debate not part of Wilsonianism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Municipal ownership is not addressed by the foreign-policy doctrine.

second-chamber.rationale: Bicameralism is not addressed in the doctrine.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-setting norms are not addressed in the doctrine.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is anachronistic to the doctrine.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is anachronistic to the doctrine.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Digital payments are anachronistic to the doctrine.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online identity is anachronistic to the doctrine.

person-over-state.rationale: Personalist philosophy is not part of the doctrine.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federal devolution is not addressed by the doctrine.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is anachronistic to the doctrine.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is not addressed by the doctrine.

racial-pride.rationale: Wilsonian doctrine does not address pride in race or ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Wilson accepted collective enforcement and war for democracy beyond narrow defence; split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Points IX, X, XIII draw frontiers along national lines; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Higher-education finance is not addressed by the doctrine.

arms-reduction.rationale: Point IV of the Fourteen Points states exactly this as a condition of lasting peace.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Point I demands open covenants openly arrived at and diplomacy in public view.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is anachronistic to the 1918 doctrine and the sources never mention it, so no lean is inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the Progressive reform temper of the New Freedom, which included conservation; the foreign-policy sources do not discuss duties to the unborn.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Wilson came to back suffrage as a war measure, but the doctrine says nothing on women's distinct values, so none is inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Point III of the Fourteen Points calls for removing economic barriers and equal trade conditions among nations, which points away from state control of cross-border flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Point IV calls for reducing national armaments to the lowest level consistent with domestic safety, implying state control of force; private armies are not discussed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Wilson led the US into war on conscription and defended obedience to duty; collective security itself relies on states fighting aggressors. Inferred from the doctrine's logic.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the Progressive New Freedom liberalism of Wilson's domestic program; the foreign-policy doctrine does not address labour.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the doctrine's scope; Progressive reformism gives no clear lean.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents have no distinctive position on borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Point III seeks equal trade conditions and removal of barriers among all nations, a liberal order of equal rules, not one tilted in favour of developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Wilsonianism holds democracy is the most virtuous government and advances reform through constitutional means and international law; Wilson opposed revolutionary upheaval.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: Wilsonians promote a common liberal democratic and open-trade order rather than diverse local economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine is silent on natural capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Wilsonian self-determination values nations but within a civic, democratic and internationalist frame, not as a sacred community; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Outside the doctrine's scope and era; no basis for a lean.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the liberal democratic view that citizens in a state share equal rights; the Fourteen Points concern colonies abroad, not regions within states.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Wilson's universalist moral language of principle and rights for all peoples; redesigning human nature is not addressed.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; Wilson's wartime Committee on Public Information was state propaganda, and the doctrine takes no clear position on independent broadcasters.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Wilson was a devout Presbyterian, but the doctrine is about foreign policy and takes no position on religious truth; neutral is inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the New Freedom's Progressive reform temper, which favoured public rural credit; the doctrine itself says nothing on farm policy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The Fourteen Points call for mutual reduction of armaments, not unilateral disarmament, and nuclear arms postdate the doctrine, so the answer is split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from Progressive liberalism, which sought reform within the existing parties rather than class-based parties; not addressed by the doctrine.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the doctrine's moral universalism and concern for the rights of persons, though Wilson never addressed it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from liberal equality-before-law principles and Progressive-era suffrage reform; not addressed in the foreign-policy doctrine.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The doctrine's self-determination of nationalities does not address how to count languages, so neutral is inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from New Freedom Progressivism, which favoured public regulation of business over private lawsuits; the doctrine is silent.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Wilson treated democratic government as the most virtuous form, so an official legislative role for hereditary or customary chiefs is inferred to be disfavoured.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; Wilsonianism is about foreign affairs and its liberal creed gives no clear ranking of environment against liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from Progressive-era penal reform, which favoured judicial and parole discretion over fixed terms; the doctrine itself is silent.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from Wilson's wartime Americanization campaign, which stressed a common language for immigrants; not part of the foreign-policy doctrine as scoped.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Wilson's New Freedom favoured some labour protection but the doctrine is foreign-policy and anachronistic on this issue.

voter-id.rationale: The doctrine does not address domestic election administration, and the issue is anachronistic.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Self-determination and liberal principles imply equal standing among faiths, but the Fourteen Points do not address religion within states.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Wilsonians treat democracy as the most virtuous government and tie it to self-government by consent, which is inferred as accepting free elections as the test, though they also expect democracies to pursue liberal ends.

premarital-sex.rationale: The doctrine is silent, and Wilson's own Presbyterian morality conflicts with its liberal reading.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Open diplomacy, freedom of the seas and free trade imply a preference for open communication; the technology is anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not a Wilsonian concern and the New Freedom predates the idea.

women-suffrage.rationale: Treating democracy as the most virtuous government implies broad participation, though the Fourteen Points do not mention women and Wilson came to suffrage late.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not a Wilsonian concern, and mainstream liberal Protestant sentiment of the period would reject it; this is inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The doctrine is silent, and Wilson's own racial views make a typical adherent's position unclear.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the doctrine; no stance can be inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not a Wilsonian concern; the doctrine is about foreign policy and Progressive liberalism gives no clear answer.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: collective security and a league of nations imply accountability for aggressors, but criminal tribunals post-date the doctrine.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Wilson was a devout Presbyterian, but Wilsonianism as doctrine is silent on biblical literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Anachronistic: the doctrine's self-determination concerned nations, not gender guarantees in self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: Wilsonianism favours democracy and freer trade and opposed Bolshevik systems, so defending a planned state is unlikely.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its view of democracy as the most virtuous government and government by consent of the governed.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from liberal principles of equal liberty; religious establishment is not addressed in the sources.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Fourteen Points give the peoples of Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman empire the freest opportunity of autonomous development.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Point V and the territorial points insist that the interests of the populations concerned weigh equally in settling claims, in line with self-determination.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Point V concerns adjusting colonial claims with regard to populations; the doctrine says nothing on postcolonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from its support for freer trade and commerce; lifestyle is not addressed.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its liberal, free-movement and trade orientation; indigenous settlement is not addressed.

equal-conscription.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed and no principle points either way.

missingStatements.text: Armaments should be reduced to the lowest level consistent with domestic safety.
missingStatements.rationale: Point IV of the Fourteen Points states exactly this as a condition of lasting peace.

missingStatements.text: Treaties and diplomacy between governments should be conducted openly, with no secret international agreements.
missingStatements.rationale: Point I demands open covenants openly arrived at and diplomacy in public view.

notes: Source access was limited: several Avalon and State Department pages returned 404, so the war message of 1917 was not opened. Scholars dispute whether Wilson was an idealist or a 'higher realist', and his own race record contrasts with the doctrine's universalism.
